# cpanel_ssl_certificate (Resource)

Manages one stored cPanel SSL certificate that is not installed on a domain. Terraform uploads only the public certificate and never reads or stores private keys. Import, update, and destroy refuse certificates that cPanel reports as configured or installed.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cpanel_ssl_certificate" "example" {
  friendly_name = "Example public certificate"
  certificate   = file("${path.module}/certificate.pem")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `certificate` (String) Exactly one PEM-encoded public X.509 certificate. Private keys and additional PEM blocks are rejected before any cPanel request. Changing the X.509 certificate replaces the resource.
- `friendly_name` (String) The display name stored by cPanel for the certificate.

### Read-Only

- `created` (Number) The certificate creation time reported by cPanel as a Unix timestamp.
- `domain_is_configured` (Boolean) Whether cPanel reports a configured domain for the stored certificate. This resource refuses management when the value is true.
- `domains` (Set of String) The certificate domains reported by cPanel.
- `fingerprint_sha256` (String) The lowercase SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate DER bytes.
- `id` (String) The certificate identifier assigned by cPanel.
- `installed` (Boolean) Whether cPanel reports the certificate on an installed SSL virtual host. This resource refuses management when the value is true.
- `is_self_signed` (Boolean) Whether cPanel reports the certificate as self-signed.
- `issuer_common_name` (String) The certificate issuer common name.
- `key_algorithm` (String) The certificate public-key algorithm reported by cPanel.
- `modulus_length` (Number) The public-key modulus length reported by cPanel, when applicable.
- `not_after` (Number) The certificate validity end as a Unix timestamp.
- `not_before` (Number) The certificate validity start as a Unix timestamp.
- `serial` (String) The certificate serial reported by cPanel.
- `signature_algorithm` (String) The certificate signature algorithm reported by cPanel.
- `subject_common_name` (String) The certificate subject common name.
- `validation_type` (String) The validation type reported by cPanel, when present.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import cpanel_ssl_certificate.example certificate-id-from-cpanel
```
